speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with a generalized nonpruritic rash and a recent history of high fever and seizure; could you tell me your age and the specific duration of these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Varicella (Chickenpox). The clinical presentation of a generalized, non-pruritic rash spreading from trunk to extremities following a high fever and seizure in an infant with up-to-date immunizations is highly suggestive of varicella, which can sometimes present with atypical or non-pruritic lesions and be associated with febrile seizures.
